name: Well Done Suite Connector
author: welldonesuite

sections.description:
Well Done Suite is a hosted console a business runs its day from: enquiries, quotes, invoices, support requests, bookings and the website. This plugin connects a WordPress site to it, so the site and its WooCommerce shop are managed in the same place as the rest of the work.

What the console can do with your site

  • Pages and posts. Read posts, pages and other public content types, create and update them, and move them to the trash.
  • WooCommerce catalogue. Read products and variations, create draft products — including hidden virtual products that stand for services sold through quotes and bookings — and update names, descriptions, prices, SKU, stock, status, categories, tags, images and their alt text, attributes, cross-sells, upsells, bundles and the SEO title and description.
  • Shop orders. See WooCommerce orders next to the orders kept in the console and move them along: change the status, add order notes and record tracking. WooCommerce sends its usual customer emails.
  • Media. Add images and PDF files to the media library.
  • Forms. Place enquiry forms, bookings, reservations and quote calculators built in the console on any page with the [welldosu_form slug="…"] shortcode.
  • Customer portal. Optional and off by default. The WooCommerce My Account page shows a customer’s shop orders next to the quotes, invoices, support requests and bookings the business keeps in the console. Sign-in, registration and passwords stay in WordPress.

What it never does

The connector answers a fixed set of REST endpoints and nothing else. It never:

  • creates, reads or changes other WordPress users;
  • changes WordPress settings;
  • installs, activates or updates plugins or themes, or downloads and runs code;
  • creates, refunds, reprices or deletes orders;
  • deletes anything permanently. Content can only go to the trash, and products and variations are never deleted.

Every change is checked against the WordPress permissions of the administrator who approved the connection. The connector does not log in as that administrator or anyone else. New content is attributed to them; existing content keeps its author.

Two screens under Settings

  • Well Done Suite connects or disconnects the site and switches the customer portal on or off.
  • Well Done Suite — Overview lists every REST endpoint, the data it returns and how it is protected.

Nothing is sent anywhere until an administrator clicks Connect to Well Done Suite.

External services

This plugin connects to Well Done Suite, a hosted service operated by Well Done Suite Ltd. The service is required: connecting the site to it is the plugin’s only purpose.

Pairing. When an administrator clicks Connect, the browser opens https://app.welldonesuite.com/wp-connect with the site address, a WordPress administrator return address and a random, single-use code that expires after five minutes. The administrator signs in to Well Done Suite and approves the connection. https://api.welldonesuite.com then sends a tenant identifier and a site-specific shared secret to the site’s POST /wp-json/wds/v1/pair endpoint. WordPress accepts them only when the code is valid and unused and the administrator who started pairing still has the manage_options capability.

Signed requests. After pairing, the service sends HTTPS requests to the connector’s endpoints. Each carries a current timestamp and an HMAC-SHA256 signature made with the shared secret, and every write is locked against replay. Depending on the console screen in use, the service receives:

  • The connector, WordPress, PHP and WooCommerce versions, and which features the site supports.
  • Content from public, REST-enabled post types: title, body, excerpt, status, author ID, dates and address, including drafts and private or trashed items when a signed request asks for them.
  • The site name, tagline, address, language, time zone, date and time format and first day of the week.
  • The login, display name, roles and a fixed list of permission flags of the administrator who approved the connection (no email address).
  • With WooCommerce active, the product catalogue (names, descriptions, SKUs, prices, stock, categories, tags, images with alt text, variations, attributes, cross-sells, upsells, bundles, SEO titles and descriptions, and addresses) and orders. Order data includes order and customer identifiers, status, totals, payment-method labels, billing name, company, email address, country, city and postcode, line items, dates, customer notes, order notes and tracking, but never payment card, bank-account or gateway credential data.

The service can also create and update content, move content to the trash, create draft products, update product details, upload an image or PDF to the media library, and change an order’s status, add an order note or record its tracking. A product image given as a web address outside the site is downloaded by WordPress into the media library, using WordPress’s own safe download and image checks, and reused afterwards. An optional idempotency key lets the service safely retry a successful write for up to 24 hours.

Disconnecting. When the administrator clicks Disconnect, the plugin sends the tenant identifier and a signed revocation request to https://api.welldonesuite.com, then deletes the local connection credentials.

Forms. Only pages that contain the [welldosu_form slug="…"] shortcode are affected:

  • When such a page is shown, WordPress asks https://api.welldonesuite.com/m/{tenant identifier}/{form name}/status whether the form is switched on. Only the tenant identifier and the form name are sent. The answer is cached for five minutes.
  • The visitor’s browser loads the form in an iframe from https://api.welldonesuite.com/m/{tenant identifier}/{form name}, together with the address of the page the form is on so the site owner can see where a submission came from. Like any web request, this sends the visitor’s IP address and browser details to the service.
  • When the visitor sends the form, the answers they typed — which may include their name, email address, phone number, message, a chosen appointment time and a consent choice — are sent to Well Done Suite and stored for the site owner. The IP address is used, as a keyed hash, only to limit repeated submissions. The service emails the site owner and, if the site owner switched it on, sends the visitor a confirmation email.

Customer portal. Off by default. Only when an administrator switches it on under Settings → Well Done Suite and the business switches it on in the console:

  • WordPress asks https://api.welldonesuite.com/v1/p/{tenant identifier}/connector-config for the portal design and whether the portal is switched on. This signed request sends the My Account page address, the plugin version and whether WooCommerce and the portal are switched on here. The answer is cached for five minutes.
  • When a signed-in customer opens My Account, their browser asks this site’s POST /wp-json/welldosu/v1/portal/handoff for a token signed with the shared secret. It contains the tenant identifier, the customer’s WordPress user ID, email address and display name, and expires after two minutes; the service accepts it once. The browser exchanges it at https://api.welldonesuite.com/v1/p/{tenant identifier}/auth/wp-handoff for a portal session and then loads that customer’s own records — shop orders (read from this site through the signed orders endpoint, narrowed to that customer), quotes, invoices, support requests and bookings — from https://api.welldonesuite.com/v1/p/…. Like any web request this sends the customer’s IP address and browser details.
  • Support requests and replies the customer writes in the portal, and a quote they accept there, are sent to Well Done Suite and kept for the site owner.
  • Customers who are not signed in see a sign-in form that posts to this site’s POST /wp-json/welldosu/v1/portal/login (WordPress’s wp_signon()), and, when WooCommerce allows registration on My Account, a registration form that posts to POST /wp-json/welldosu/v1/portal/register (WooCommerce’s wc_create_new_customer()). Neither sends anything to Well Done Suite; passwords never leave WordPress.

The plugin loads no remote scripts or stylesheets into WordPress. Its only front-end files are its own assets/css/mechanism.css and assets/js/mechanism-frame.js, which fits the form frame to the height the form reports, and — only on My Account with the customer portal switched on — assets/portal/portal.js and assets/portal/portal.css.

The service never receives WordPress passwords or password hashes, other users’ details, payment card or bank-account data, private keys, gateway credentials or WordPress options other than those listed above.

  • Well Done Suite service
  • Connector documentation
  • Terms of Service
  • Privacy Notice

Source code

assets/portal/portal.js and `assets/portal/portal.css` are compiled. Their complete, readable source is shipped in `assets/portal/src/`. The build bundles `assets/portal/src/portal/embed.jsx` with React 18.3.1 into one script and one stylesheet, using Vite 6.4.3 with @vitejs/plugin-react 4.3.4 in library mode with IIFE output. Every other file in the plugin is shipped as written.<h3>Credits</h3>

The settings screens use the Onest typeface, © 2021 The Onest Project Authors, licensed under the SIL Open Font License 1.1 (assets/fonts/OFL.txt).
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate Well Done Suite Connector.
  2. Go to Settings → Well Done Suite.
  3. Click Connect to Well Done Suite.
  4. Sign in to Well Done Suite and approve the named WordPress site.
  5. Continue in the Well Done Suite console. If the business has no active access yet, its owner can start the free 14-day trial or choose a monthly or annual plan there.

To disconnect, return to the same screen and click Disconnect.
sections.faq:
Is a Well Done Suite account required?

Yes, to connect the site. The Overview screen works without a connection and explains every endpoint and data category.

Can the console install or activate plugins?

No. The connector neither downloads nor runs code from Well Done Suite or any other server, and has no way to install, activate, update or remove plugins or themes.

Can the console create administrators or change users?

No. The connector has no user endpoints. The only user it reports on is the administrator who approved the connection, and only their login, display name, roles and a fixed list of permission flags.

Can the console change WordPress settings?

No. The settings endpoint is read-only and returns only the site name, tagline, address, language, time zone, date and time format and first day of the week.

Can the console change content?

Yes. It can create and update posts, pages and other public, REST-enabled content, and move them to the trash. WordPress checks the permissions of the administrator who approved the connection before every change. Permanent deletion is not available: if the WordPress trash is disabled, the connector refuses to delete and leaves the content in place.

What can it change in WooCommerce?

It can create draft products and update existing products and their listed variations: name, descriptions, prices, SKU, stock, status, categories, tags, images and their alt text, attributes, cross-sells, upsells, bundles and the SEO title and description. Publishing needs the administrator to be allowed to publish products. It never deletes products or variations.

For orders it can set the status to pending payment, on hold, processing, completed or cancelled, add an order note and record a tracking number and link. Status changes go through WooCommerce, so its customer emails and stock changes happen as they do in wp-admin; a note for the customer is emailed by WooCommerce. Each change needs the administrator to be allowed to edit shop orders. It never creates, refunds, reprices or deletes orders, and refunded or failed orders stay as the payment provider left them.

Does the plugin execute AI-generated code?

No. Assistance in the hosted console can propose a change, but this plugin only accepts its fixed REST endpoints. It never evaluates PHP, JavaScript, SQL or shell commands it receives.

Does the plugin add anything to the public site?

Only where a site editor adds the [welldosu_form] shortcode, and on the WooCommerce My Account page when the customer portal is switched on. A shortcode page shows a Well Done Suite form in an iframe (see External services). Everywhere else the plugin adds nothing to the public site: no block, no tracking script and no other visitor-facing output. While a form is switched off, visitors see nothing and editors see a short note.

How do I switch the customer portal on or off?

Under Settings → Well Done Suite, use Use the customer portal on My Account, and switch it on for the shop in the console under Customer portal → Where the portal runs. While either is off — or if the service cannot be reached — My Account shows the standard WooCommerce page. Adding ?welldosu_classic=1 to the My Account address always shows the standard page.

Connecting says “Connection request expired”. What now?

The one-time code created when you click Connect lasts five minutes. Go back to Settings → Well Done Suite, click Connect again and finish the approval straight away.

What happens when the site is disconnected?

The local tenant identifier, shared secret and administrator reference are deleted, and the service is told to forget the connection. Signed requests then fail.

Does it support multisite?

Each site in a network can be connected separately. Network-wide connection is not supported. Uninstalling removes the connector’s data from every site.
sections.changelog:
0.6.1

  • Product updates from the console can now set cross-sells and upsells (by SKU), attributes — shared attributes for the ones shoppers filter by, product-only attributes for the rest of the specification — the SEO title and meta description, alt text on the product’s images, and a bundle of products with a discount. Attributes that make variations are never changed.
  • The SEO title and description are kept in the connector’s own product fields, and also written to Yoast SEO, Rank Math or SEOPress when that plugin is active. Other plugins’ fields are never touched while they are inactive. With no SEO plugin active, the connector prints the title and description on the product page itself.
  • A product read now includes its cross-sells, upsells, attributes, SEO fields and bundle, so the console can tell what the shop already holds.
  • New shared attributes and attribute values are created only when the administrator who connected the site may manage WooCommerce and product terms.

0.6.0

  • Shop orders can be moved along from the console: status (pending payment, on hold, processing, completed or cancelled), order notes and tracking, through the new signed PATCH /wds/v1/orders/{id}. Status changes go through WooCommerce, so its customer emails and stock changes happen as in wp-admin. Each change needs the administrator who connected the site to be allowed to edit shop orders. Orders are still never created, refunded, repriced or deleted.
  • One order now comes with its order notes, and every order with the tracking recorded in the console.
  • The suggested privacy-policy text and the Overview screen now list every site setting the connector reads, including the time format and the first day of the week.

Earlier versions are listed in changelog.txt.
